  CITY OF SANTA MONICA

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  MAY 12, 2020

A regular meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor McKeown at 5:30 p.m., on
Tuesday, May 12, 2020, via teleconference pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20 at
https://primetime.bluejeans.com/a2m/live-event/qabdpbgt.

Roll Call:  Present:  Mayor Kevin McKeown
  Mayor Pro Tem Terry O’Day
  Councilmember Gleam Davis
  Councilmember Sue Himmelrich
  Councilmember Ana M. Jara
  Councilmember Greg Morena
  Councilmember Ted Winterer

  Also Present:  Interim City Manager Lane Dilg
  Interim City Attorney George Cardona
  City Clerk Denise Anderson-Warren

CONVENE  On order of the Mayor, the City Council convened at 5:33p.m., with all
  members present.

CLOSED SESSIONS  There was no one present for public comment on closed sessions.

  On order of the Mayor, the City Council recessed at 5:33 p.m., to consider
  closed sessions and returned at 7:25 p.m., with all members present, to
  report the following:

  1.A. Conference with Labor Negotiator: Government Code Section
  54957.6
  Agency Designated Representatives: Chief People Officer Lori Gentles
  and Human Resources Manager Shawn Weiske. Bargaining Units:
  Administrative Team Associates, California Teamsters Local 911,
  Confidential Unrepresented Employees Pay Plan, Executive Pay Plan,
  Municipal Employees Association, Management Team Associates,
  Public Attorneys Legal Support Staff Union, Public Attorneys Union,
  Santa Monica Fire Executive Management Association, Santa Monica
  Firefighters Local 1109 IAFF, Santa Monica Police Officers
  Association, Supervisory Team Associates, International Association of
  Sheet Metal, Air, Rail, and Transportation Workers, Transportation
  Division Local 1785 (SMART TD).

  1  May 12, 2020
   The Interim City Attorney advised this matter was heard with no reportable
  action taken.

  1.B. Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation –
  Litigation has been initiated formally pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54956.9(d)(1): Shawn Joyner v. City of Santa Monica, Ernesto
  Rodriquez, Los Angeles Superior Court, Case BC599994.

  The Interim City Attorney advised this matter was an injury that occurred
  on the Big Blue Bus. The City Attorney’s Office recommended a
  Settlement Agreement in the amount of $350,000.

  Motion by Councilmember Davis, seconded by Councilmember
  Himmelrich, to approve Settlement Agreement No. 11043 (CCS). The
  motion was approved by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Jara, Winterer, Davis, Himmelrich, Morena,
  Mayor Pro Tem O’Day, Mayor McKeown
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

CONSENT CALENDAR:  All items were considered and approved in one motion unless removed by a
  Councilmember for discussion.

  There was no public comment on the various Consent Calendar items.

  At the request of Councilmember Morena, Item 3.E was removed from the
  Consent Calendar.

  Motion by Councilmember Jara, seconded by Councilmember Morena, to
  approve the Consent Calendar except for Item 3.E., reading resolutions by
  title only and waiving further reading thereof. The motion was approved
  by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Jara, Winterer, Davis, Himmelrich, Morena,
  Mayor Pro Tem O’Day, Mayor McKeown
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

FOURTH STREET EXPO  3.A. Approval of Contract Modification for Additional Design
  Services to Obtain Caltrans Clearance for the Fourth Street Expo
  Linkages Project, was approved.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute a first

  2  May 12, 2020
   modification to agreement #10674 (CCS) in the amount of
  $130,000 with Cannon Corporation, a California-based company,
  for additional design and coordination services for an enhanced
  Fourth Street bridge barrier treatment required by Caltrans for the
  Fourth Street Pedestrian and Bicycle Improvements/Expo Linkages
  Phase II project. This would result in a four-year amended
  agreement with a new total amount not to exceed $445,000
  ($280,000 of the total is state grant-funded by Caltrans’ Active
  Transportation Program);
  2. Authorize budget changes as outlined in the Financial Impacts and
  Budget Actions section of this report.

BIG BLUE BUS  3.B. Authorization to enter into Agreement No. 11038 (CCS) with
  UCLA for Extension of BruinGO Transit Pass Program, was approved.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to
  negotiate and execute an agreement to renew the Big Blue Bus Transit Pass
  Program (BruinGo!) with the University of California, Los Angeles
  (UCLA) effective July 1, 2020 for a three-year term through June 30, 2023
  with two, one-year, mutually agreed upon options through June 30, 2025 at
  the costs noted in the Negotiated Rates section of the staff report.

TOWING SERVICES  3.C.  Award Bid for Towing Services, was approved.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Award Bid #4388 to:
  a) FMG Inc. (a California-based company) for towing services for the
  City’s fleet of transit buses and heavy-duty fire apparatus;
  b) Classic Tow, Inc., doing business as Tip Top Tow Service (a
  California-based company) for towing of the City’s fleet of
  passenger and light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, Police
  department vehicles, and towing and storage of impounded vehicles
  for the City’s Police Department; and,
  c) EVS Inc. doing business as All City Tow Service (a California-
  based company), for towing and storage of impounded vehicles for
  the City’s Police Department;
  2. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute Agreement Nos.
  11039 (CCS) through 11041 (CCS) with:
  a) FMG Inc for towing of transit buses and Fire Department heavy
  apparatus in an amount not to exceed $532,030 over a five-year
  period, which includes a 10% contingency and a 5% cost escalator
  in year 5, with future year funding contingent on Council budget
  approval; and
  b) Classic Tow, Inc., for passenger and light, medium, and heavy-duty

  3  May 12, 2020
   vehicle towing and impounding services in an amount not to exceed
  $1,609,350 over a five-year period, which includes a 10%
  contingency and a 5% annual cost escalator, with future year
  funding contingent on Council budget approval; and
  c) EVS Inc., for light-duty, medium-duty, and heavy-duty towing and
  storage of impounded vehicles in an amount not to exceed $27,500
  over a five-year period, which includes a 10% contingency with
  future year funding contingent on Council budget approval.

INTERIM CITY  3.D. Approval of Agreement No. 11042 (CCS) with George Cardona
ATTORNEY  for his services as Interim City Attorney, was approved.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that Council:
  (1) approve the agreement with George Cardona for his services as
  Interim City Attorney; and,
  (2) authorize the Mayor to sign the agreement on behalf of the City.

COVID-19 EMERGENCY  3.E. Adoption of Resolution No. 11247 (CCS) entitled “AN
  EMERGENCY RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF SANTA MONICA PURSUANT TO CHAPTER 2.16 OF THE SANTA
  MONICA MUNICIPAL CODE RATIFYING THE PROCLAMATION OF
  EXISTENCE OF LOCAL EMERGENCY AND SUPPLEMENTAL
  PROCLAMATIONS THERETO”, was presented.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that Council adopt the attached resolution ratifying the
  Executive Order issued by the Director of Emergency Services declaring
  the existence of a local emergency in the city of Santa Monica and the
  Supplements to that Order.

  Councilmember Morena pulled this item to recuse himself to avoid any
  appearance of a conflict of interest because his family owns a restaurant on
  the Pier.
Councilmember Morena
excused at 7:28 p.m.  Motion by Mayor Pro Tem O’Day, seconded by Councilmember Jara, to
  approve the recommended action. The motion was approved by the
  following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Himmelrich, Davis, Winterer, Jara,
  Mayor Pro Tem O’Day, Mayor McKeown
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: Councilmember Morena

ORDINANCES:  7.A. Second Reading and Adoption of Ordinance No. 2635 (CCS)
BUILDING STANDARDS  entitled, “AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY

  4  May 12, 2020
 Councilmember Morena  OF SANTA MONICA AMENDING SECTION 8.08.050 OF THE SANTA
returned at 7:30 p.m.  MONICA MUNICIPAL CODE TO ADOPT THE 2019 CALIFORNIA
  BUILDING STANDARDS CODE REGULATION TO EXEMPT
  FREESTANDING WALLS SEVEN FEET OR LESS IN HEIGHT FROM
  REQUIRING A BUILDING PERMIT, AND ADOPT A LOCAL
  AMENDMENT TO THE BUILDING STANDARDS CODE TO
  EXEMPT CONCRETE OR MASONRY WALLS FOUR FEET IN
  HEIGHT OR LESS FROM REQUIRING A BUILDING PERMIT”, was
  presented.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that City Council adopt the attached Ordinance.

  Motion by Councilmember Himmelrich, seconded by Councilmember
  Morena, to adopt the ordinance, reading by title only and waiving further
  reading thereof. The motion was approved by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Jara, Winterer, Davis, Himmelrich, Morena,
  Mayor Pro Tem O’Day, Mayor McKeown
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

ZONING  7.B. Introduction and Adoption of Emergency Interim Zoning
  Ordinance No. 2636 (CCS) entitled “AN EMERGENCY INTERIM
  ZONING ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  SANTA MONICA ESTABLISHING INTERIM ZONING
  REGULATIONS FOR ECONOMIC RECOVERY OF THE BC
  (PROMENADE) DISTRICT AND THOSE PORTIONS OF THE BC
  (2ND AND 4TH STREET) DISTRICT BOUNDED BY SECOND
  STREET TO THE WEST, BROADWAY TO THE SOUTH, 4TH
  STREET TO THE EAST, AND WILSHIRE BOULEVARD TO THE
  NORTH”, was presented.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt an Emergency Interim
  Zoning Ordinance establishing interim zoning regulations to support and
  facilitate the economic recovery of the Third Street Promenade area,
  bounded by 2nd Street to the west, Broadway to the south, 4th Street to the
  east, and Wilshire Boulevard to the north.

  Members of the public Denise Barton and Shawn Landres commented on
  the recommended action.

  Questions asked and answered of staff included: what are the negative
  consequences for having permanent land use entitlements; what used to
  happen with the loading requirements previously; with the activation of the

  5  May 12, 2020
 alleys, is there going to cause any problems with loading; what’s going to
happen with non-appeal option for alcohol exemptions if the city receives
complaints from residents in the area; is there another alternative for people
who live on the Promenade to get notification that an alcohol exemption is
being issued; besides a citations, can some other penalty be brought against
an establishment for violation; would this allow the Planning Director to
approve a tasting room if it is not in the code; don’t establishments have
Department of Alcohol Beverage Control licenses which already require
them to have a large percentage of food sales; how is the loading in the
alley going to affect automobile and non-automobile access; in determining
what access is available, will this allow the Planning Director to look at
better usage for space; is there some way that complaints can be reviewed
post opening to see if operators are acting in bad faith; what’s the on-going
process going forward when tweaks are needed; is there a timeframe for the
loading, is there something already in place to address impacts, for example
sanitation; has there been any complaints since the issuance of alcohol-
exemption permits; will this plan allow inadvertently a combination of
spaces or will there still be limitations on how space can be used; is there
anything in this that allows creativity to office space on the ground floor;
why not temporarily suspend rules, instead of abandoning them completely
which would leave the city with no recourse if a restaurant changes uses;
and, with the alcohol provision, is the city able to enforce the law.

Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to,
consider our permitting fees and what a reduction in those would yield in
terms of activity, and, look for ways to provide non-car travel.

Motion by Councilmember Davis, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem O’Day, to
introduce and adopt at first reading of the emergency ordinance reading by
title only and waiving further reading thereof.

Mayor McKeown proposed an amendment to change the cap to 50 percent
on alcohol sales to be in accordance with the Department of Alcohol
Beverage Control rules, and rather than having a one-year limit to three-
year limit for any reuse of a site/business. The motion was not considered
friendly by the maker or seconder.

Substitute motion by Mayor McKeown, to retain the recommendation and
to add the two previous amendments. The motion died due to lack of a
second.

Councilmember Himmelrich, proposed a friendly amendment to adopt the
Department of Alcohol Beverage Control’s requirement, if only to make it
within the city’s ability to enforce it. The motion was withdrawn because
this provision is already included in the proposed ordinance.

  6  May 12, 2020
   The motion was approved by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Morena, Himmelrich, Davis, Jara, Winterer,
  Mayor Pro Tem O’Day, Mayor McKeown
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  Direction given to staff to prioritize looking for creative ways to let
  restaurants expand their serving footprint by using space that might not
  otherwise be available to them such as sufficiently wide sidewalks, closed-
  off street areas or nearby parking lots.

ECONOMIC RECOVERY  7.C. Introduction and Adoption of Emergency Interim Zoning
  Ordinance No. 2637 (CCS) entitled “AN EMERGENCY INTERIM
  ZONING ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  SANTA MONICA ESTABLISHING INTERIM ZONING
  REGULATIONS FOR ECONOMIC RECOVERY IN THE CITY’S
  DOWNTOWN, MIXED USE AND COMMERCIAL, EMPLOYMENT,
  OCEANFRONT, AND PUBLIC AND SEMI-PUBLIC DISTRICTS,
  EXCLUDING THE AREA INCLUDING AND IMMEDIATELY
  ADJACENT TO THE THIRD STREET PROMENADE SUBJECT TO
  DIFFERENT INTERIM ZONING REGULATIONS”, was presented.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council introduce and adopt an Emergency
  Interim Zoning Ordinance modifying permitting procedures and use
  classifications to support the economic recovery of local business impacted
  by COVID-19 in all commercial areas except for the Third Street
  Promenade area.

  Member of the public Joshua Lickman spoke to the recommended action.

  Questions asked and answered of staff included: why the difference in
  hours for serving alcohol from 2 a.m. to midnight; is this blanket closing at
  midnight to streamline and simplify; if a restaurant wanted to stay open
  until 2 a.m. would they be able to do that through the CUP process; does
  looking at outdoor dining include looking at restaurants expanding their
  serving space to allow for social distancing; is the extension of the one-year
  applicability retroactive; is there a reason the light industry was included on
  Third Street, but not on Main Street; is a to-go window with limited service
  included; why wasn’t Bergamot included and are there any other areas of
  the city that should be included in the new rules; any reason why tattoo
  shops, barber shops or salons weren’t included; does this IZO allow
  different businesses to fit a round peg into a square box; what was the
  thinking behind the no standing on outside patio restriction; was the letter
  from the Main Street Merchants with their additional ideas received and

  7  May 12, 2020
 considered; and, was the letter received from a large property owner in the
Bergamot area regarding parking requirements received and considered.

Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to:
Main Street restaurants that served alcohol up to 2 a.m. have drawn a lot of
complaints in the past; although there are suitable places, not every
establishment on Main Street should be able to serve alcohol until 2 a.m.; if
an operator wants to serve alcohol until 2 a.m., they can apply for a CUP
which will allow neighbors the opportunity to weigh in with any concerns;
a CUP would allow the Planning Commission to craft conditions that
addresses any concerns; concerns that new businesses will be treated
differently than existing businesses on Main Street; concerns that the City
may be undervaluing adjacent residential neighborhoods and ignoring
serious impacts to those who live close by; the financial viability of alcohol
sales, especially between midnight and 2 a.m.

Motion by Councilmember Winterer, seconded by Councilmember Jara, to
introduce and adopt at first reading of the emergency ordinance reading by
title only and waiving further reading thereof.

Councilmember Davis proposed a friendly amendment to pay special
attention to the interaction between loading operations and, in general,
potential conflicts between automobiles and other forms of transportation
such as pick-up zones and cars crossing the bike lanes. The motion was
considered friendly by the maker and the seconder.

Councilmember Morena proposed a friendly amendment to include tattoo
shops and personal care sites in the IZO. The motion was not considered
friendly by the maker.

Councilmember Morena proposed a friendly amendment to offer the
alcohol exemptions for Friday and Saturday nights extending until 2 a.m.
The motion was not considered friendly by the maker.

A substitute motion by Councilmember Morena, seconded by Mayor Pro
Tem O’Day to adopt the recommendation, with the friendly amendment by
Councilmember Davis, and include the alcohol exemptions for Friday and
Saturday nights extending until 2 am.

The motion failed by the following vote:

AYES: Councilmembers Morena, Davis, Mayor Pro Tem O’Day
NOES: Councilmembers Himmelrich, Winterer, Jara, Mayor McKeown
ABSENT: None

  8  May 12, 2020
   The main motion was back on the floor, including the friendly amendment
  from Councilmember Davis.

  Motion by Councilmember Winterer, seconded by Councilmember Jara, to
  introduce and adopt at first reading of the emergency ordinance reading by
  title only and waiving further reading thereof, with the amendment as we
  go through this plan, paying special attention to the interaction between
  loading operations and potential conflicts between automobiles and other
  forms of transportation. The motion was approved by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Jara, Winterer, Davis, Himmelrich, Morena,
  Mayor Pro Tem O’Day, Mayor McKeown
  NOES:  None

 SHARED MOBILITY  7.E. Introduction and First Reading of an Ordinance Modification
  to Postpone Launch Date of the Second Shared Mobility Pilot Program
  and Restructure PROW Fees, was presented.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1) Introduce for first reading the proposed ordinance, amending Section
  3.21.090 of the Santa Monica Municipal Code to extend the term of
  the first Shared Mobility Device Pilot Program from June 30, 2020
  to September 13, 2020, and amending Section 3.22.090 of the Santa
  Monica Municipal Code to change the effective date of permits for
  the second Shared Mobility Pilot Program from July 1, 2020 to
  September 14, 2020.
  2) Provide direction to staff on the restructuring of the established $1
  per device per day PROW fee to a per trip PROW fee.

  Members of the public Tim Harder and David Fairbank spoke to the
  recommended action.

  Questions asked and answered of staff included: which operators are left in
  the city and what kind of devices are they using; when does the Breeze bike
  contract terminate; does it make senses to do the micro-mobility proposals
  in September to bridge the gap between the end of the Breeze contract and
  the other mobility companies; are public-right-of-way fees being
  considered for other delivery services or is it just applicable to micro-
  mobility; when was the original RFA due; how long does this program last;
  what’s the revenue for devices over the past year; if the similar amount of
  numbers were applied for ridership, what would the revenue be using the
  per trip fee; where did the question of mopeds end up with regard to micro-
  mobility; where is the $1 going for infrastructure today; if the operator fee
  is reduced in half, would that be enough to recoup our cost; where does the
  city stand on mopeds and what are operators supposed to do if they are not
  included; how long would it take to develop a plan for moped operators to
  be included in the shared mobility plan; has there been any thought about
  delaying this RFA proposal and just treading lightly and wait for things to
  rebound a little from the COVID-19; is there any sense why the previous
  scooter and bike companies left the city; on the bidder call, what types of
  devices did the various companies have to offer; do other cities around
  charge a per trip fee, and if they do, how much do they charge; have there
  been any comparisons for insurance requirements; can we amend the pilot
  program as it currently exists to sub other operators; is it possible to take
  the allocation and split it among the remaining two entities; and, what
  happens when the Breeze bike contract is up in November.

  Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to: how
  to get affordable, equitable transportation to local residents; given this time

  10  May 12, 2020
   of uncertainty, extend the program a year to work out a lot of questions,
  concerns and address the uncertainty; and, Breeze should be incorporated in
  with shared mobility.

  Motion by Councilmember Davis, seconded by Councilmember Morena, to
  introduce and hold first reading of the ordinance reading by title only and
  waiving further reading thereof, with a change to extend the current pilot
  program with the two current operators for a term through April 30, 2021;
  direct staff to come back with a proposal to change the fee structure; and
  give time to figure out how integrating the future of the Breeze Bike
  Sharing program into the planning process.

  Councilmember Himmelrich proposed a friendly amendment to consider
  including mopeds to shared mobility devices and direct staff to come back
  with a per-trip fee instead of a per-day fee. The motion was considered
  friendly by the maker and seconder.

  The motion, with amendments was approved by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Jara, Winterer, Davis, Himmelrich, Morena,
